t: The Persian fleet, probably fewer than a third of Herodotus's 300 ships after the Phoenician ships were dismissed, was beached below Mycale and fenced with a palisade, and the Greeks attacked it there by landing their marines.
The Ionian Greek contingents in the Persian army turned on the Persians during the fighting, though Joshua Nudell argues this betrayal is overstated and perhaps invented.
Together with Plataea, the battle ended the second Persian invasion of Greece, and the Greeks then went over to the offensive.
dyk: Richard Evans notes that Mycale was the first battle in recorded history fought on a beach, and he estimates that the strip of beach was only 20 to 30 metres long at low tide.
ev: A Persian army under Xerxes defeats the Greeks at Thermopylae and Artemisium, and the Greek navy wins at Salamis
The Greek fleet of about 110 ships gathers at Aegina under the Spartan king Leotychides and moves to Delos
A delegation from Samos tells the Greeks that the Ionian cities are ready to revolt, and the fleet sails for Samos
The Persians withdraw from Samos and beach their fleet below Mycale behind a palisaded camp
The Greeks land, defeat the Persian force and burn its ships
The Greek fleet sails to the Hellespont and finds the pontoon bridges destroyed, and the Athenians besiege Sestos
Chios, Lesbos and Samos join the Hellenic alliance

f.date: 27 or 28 August 479 BCE, the afternoon of the same day as the Battle of Plataea according to Paul A. Rahe; Charles Hignett proposes late August
f.place: The slopes of Mount Mycale on the coast of Ionia, opposite the island of Samos, in present-day Turkey; the exact site is disputed
f.sides: An alliance of Greek city-states including Sparta, Athens and Corinth, under the Spartan king Leotychides, against the Persian Empire of Xerxes I, whose land force was led by Tigranes and whose fleet was led by Artaÿntes; the strengths on both sides are disputed
f.outcome: The Persian troops were routed and their camp stormed, and the Persian ships were captured and burned. Tigranes and Mardontes were killed, while Artaÿntes and Ithamitres escaped.
